units.text: INT. DOLLHOUSE - CONTINUOUS
[SCENE.—A room furnished comfortably and tastefully, but not extravagantly.
At the back, a door to the right leads to the entrance-hall, another to the left leads to Helmer’s study.
Between the doors stands a piano.
In the middle of the left-hand wall is a door, and beyond it a window.
Near the window are a round table, arm-chairs and a small sofa.
In the right-hand wall, at the farther end, another door; and on the same side, nearer the footlights, a stove, two easy chairs and a rocking-chair; between the stove and the door, a small table.
Engravings on the walls; a cabinet with china and other small objects; a small book-case with well-bound books.
The floors are carpeted, and a fire burns in the stove.
It is winter.
A bell rings in the hall; shortly afterwards the door is heard to open.
Enter NORA, humming a tune and in high spirits.
She is in outdoor dress and carries a number of parcels; these she lays on the table to the right.
She leaves the outer door open after her, and through it is seen a PORTER who is carrying a Christmas Tree and a basket, which he gives to the MAID who has opened the door.]
Hide the Christmas Tree carefully, Helen. Be sure the children do not see it until this evening, when it is dressed.
units.name: NORA

units.text: To the PORTER, taking out her purse.
How much?
units.name: NORA

units.text: Sixpence.
units.name: PORTER

units.text: There is a shilling. No, keep the change.
units.name: NORA

units.text: The PORTER thanks her, and goes out.
NORA shuts the door.
She is laughing to herself, as she takes off her hat and coat.
She takes a packet of macaroons from her pocket and eats one or two; then goes cautiously to her husband’s door and listens.
Yes, he is in.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Still humming, she goes to the table on the right.
calls out from his room.
. Is that my little lark twittering out there?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: busy opening some of the parcels.
. Yes, it is!
units.name: NORA

units.text: Is it my little squirrel bustling about?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Yes!
units.name: NORA

units.text: When did my squirrel come home?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Just now.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Puts the bag of macaroons into her pocket and wipes her mouth.
Come in here, Torvald, and see what I have bought.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Don’t disturb me.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: A little later, he opens the door and looks into the room, pen in hand.
Bought, did you say? All these things? Has my little spendthrift been wasting money again?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Yes but, Torvald, this year we really can let ourselves go a little. This is the first Christmas that we have not needed to economise.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Still, you know, we can’t spend money recklessly.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Yes, Torvald, we may be a wee bit more reckless now, mayn’t we? Just a tiny wee bit! You are going to have a big salary and earn lots and lots of money.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Yes, after the New Year; but then it will be a whole quarter before the salary is due.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Pooh! we can borrow until then.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Nora!
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Goes up to her and takes her playfully by the ear.
The same little featherhead! Suppose, now, that I borrowed fifty pounds today, and you spent it all in the Christmas week, and then on New Year’s Eve a slate fell on my head and killed me, and—
units.name: HELMER

units.text: putting her hands over his mouth.
. Oh! don’t say such horrid things.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Still, suppose that happened,—what then?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: If that were to happen, I don’t suppose I should care whether I owed money or not.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Yes, but what about the people who had lent it?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: They? Who would bother about them? I should not know who they were.
units.name: NORA

units.text: That is like a woman! But seriously, Nora, you know what I think about that. No debt, no borrowing. There can be no freedom or beauty about a home life that depends on borrowing and debt. We two have kept bravely on the straight road so far, and we will go on the same way for the short time longer that there need be any struggle.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: moving towards the stove.
. As you please, Torvald.
units.name: NORA

units.text: following her.
. Come, come, my little skylark must not droop her wings. What is this! Is my little squirrel out of temper?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Taking out his purse.
Nora, what do you think I have got here?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: turning round quickly.
